messages:
maria: Heads up — AcmeCorp started getting 401s right after we turned on Okta SSO JIT provisioning for their org. They say nothing changed on their side other than enabling SSO. Example request they sent:

maria: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o", "input":"hi"}'
```

maria: Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` + body `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"invalid_api_key"}`

leo: Can you paste the full header they used (redact actual keys) and any server-side log lines? Also which user/email is affected so we can check DB.

maria: Pasted header (redacted): `Authorization: Bearer eyJ0eXAi...` — user email: tay+acme@acme.com

maria: Server log snippet from their request (redacted IP):
```
[auth] request_id=abc123 user_email=tay+acme@acme.com auth_type=api_key validation_error=format_mismatch token_preview="eyJhbGc..." result=401 invalid_api_key
```

sam: Quick hypothesis: Okta JIT flow returns an OIDC id_token (JWT) and our sso-provisioner service should be creating an API key and storing that, but a recent change accidentally wrote the id_token into the `api_key` column. JWTs contain dots and long base64 segments — our API key validator rejects that format.

leo: Oof. Do we have a repro locally? Can we simulate the JIT endpoint returning `id_token` and see what gets persisted?

sam: Repro steps I ran:
1) Call the JIT webhook handler with payload from Okta (includes `id_token` and `access_token`).
2) sso-provisioner created user row and set `user.api_key = payload.id_token` (bug: var name mixup).
3) Call the public API with `Authorization: Bearer <that_value>` -> 401 invalid_api_key.

sam: Bad line in code (`sso-provisioner/handlers/jit.go`):
```go
// BUG: assigning idToken instead of generated API key
user.ApiKey = payload.IdToken // should be generateAPIKey()
db.Save(&user)
```

maria: That matches the customer's timeline — they flipped SSO on and the first time we auto-provisioned the user we overwrote their API key with the JWT.

leo: Impact scope? How many orgs/users provisioned while sso-provisioner v1.3.2 was live?

sam: Quick query shows ~42 users across 9 orgs got api_key column populated with jwt-looking strings between 2026-03-10T03:00 and 2026-03-10T03:47 (deploy window). I filtered by `api_key LIKE 'eyJ.%'`.

maria: Customer-facing action: can we rotate their API key server-side and send them the new key? They urgently need a working key for prod.

sam: Plan:
- Hotfix deployed (patch in PR ready) to stop writing id_token to api_key and to validate during provisioning.
- Migration script: detect rows where `api_key` looks like a JWT (regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`) and regenerate a proper API key for those users.
- Notify affected org admins and provide instructions to re-fetch key from Console (we will push new key once migration runs).

leo: ETA for deploy + migration?

sam: Patch deploy in ~20m, migration run in maintenance window immediately after. Migration small (42 rows) — non-blocking. I'll run it and DM the support engineer assigned.

support-bot: :rotating_light: Incident draft available at https://go.redwood/incident/1256 — use template "SSO provisioning -> API key overwrite" for customer comms.

maria: Can you also add a quick fix to the dashboard to detect keys that look like JWTs and refuse to display them as API keys? We should not surface id_tokens as API keys.

sam: Agreed. Also adding unit test to sso-provisioner to assert `user.ApiKey` matches api key format and never contains dots.

maria: Customer message (draft):
```
Hi Tay,

We found the cause of the 401s: during Okta JIT provisioning a bug caused your user record to store an OIDC token (not an API key) in the API key field. We've regenerated a new API key for your account and posted it to your Console. Please log in -> Settings -> API keys to copy the new key. We apologize for the disruption; patch and validations are deployed to prevent recurrence.

If you prefer we can rotate keys for other team members — let us know.

— Maria (Support)
```

leo: Sounds good. After patch + migration, let's add a monitoring alert: rate of `invalid_api_key` per org spiking after a provisioning event.

sam: Done. I'll post when migration completes and share the audit SQL used so CS can verify.

maria: Thanks. I'll update the customer thread and mark as high-priority until they confirm keys work. :white_check_mark:
